outputs.exact_statement: Let $Y$ be either the finite-height forest dual $X=J^*$ or the infinite-height coordinate predual $B_\infty$. For every finite ancestral $H$, every $x,y\in Y$ with $x=P_Hx$, and every $R\ge0$ with $\|x+y\|,\|x-y\|\le R$, $$\label{eq:main-squared-tail} \|Q_Hy\|\le2\sqrt{R^2-\|x\|^2}.$$

The space $X$ defined by [eq:segment-norm] is infinite dimensional, separable, and reflexive, and the coordinate functionals have dense span in $X$. Let $H\subset\mathcal F$ be finite and *ancestral*, meaning that it contains every ancestor of each of its vertices. The coordinate projections $P_H$ and $Q_H$ are contractive on both $J$ and $X$. Moreover, $P_Hx\to x$ along any increasing ancestral exhaustion of $\mathcal F$.

For every finite ancestral $H$, $$\label{eq:cone-decomposition}
 Q_HJ=\left(\bigoplus_{g\in G_H}J(U_g)\right)_{\ell_2},
 \qquad
 \|Q_Hx\|^2=\sum_{g\in G_H}\|x|_{J(U_g)}\|^2\quad(x\in X).$$ The gate-coordinate map $x\mapsto(x(e_g))_{g\in G_H}$ is a contraction from $X$ to $\ell_2(G_H)$.

Let $H\subset T_\infty$ be finite and ancestral. The coordinate projections $P_H$ and $Q_H=I-P_H$ are contractive on $J_\infty$ and $B_\infty$. The range of $P_H$ is finite dimensional, and finite coefficient vectors supported outside $H$ are dense in $\ker P_H$. Along every increasing ancestral exhaustion, $P_Hx\to x$ in $B_\infty$. A nonzero vector $x=P_Hx$ has a norming test $f=P_Hf$ with $\rho(f)=1$ and $x(f)=\|x\|$.

For finite ancestral $H$, the unit ball of $P_HB_\infty$ is the convex hull of represented atoms with all segments in $H$. Each point is a convex combination of at most $|H|+1$ such atoms. The full unit ball of $B_\infty$ is the norm-closed convex hull of finite atoms.*

*On $P_HB_\infty$ the norm also equals the gauge $$\inf\left\{\sum_j\lambda_j:
   x=\sum_j\lambda_j A_j,\quad \lambda_j\ge0,\quad
   A_j\text{ atoms supported in }H\right\}.$$ In particular, a vector of norm strictly below one has such a finite representation with $\sum_j\lambda_j<1$. The gauge defined on $c_{00}(T_\infty)$ by allowing all finite atoms has the same value. Its completion is therefore isometric to $B_\infty$.

For a finite ancestral set $K$, the unit ball of $P_KX$ is the convex hull of the atoms whose segments lie in $K$. Each member is a convex combination of at most $|K|+1$ such atoms. If $0\ne x=P_Hx$ for a finite ancestral $H$, there is $p=P_Hp\in J$ with $\rho(p)=1$ and $x(p)=\|x\|$.
Let $\mathcal A$ be the set of all represented atoms in $X$. Then $$B_X=\overline{\operatorname{conv}\mathcal A}^{\,\|\cdot\|}.$$ Every segment functional $d_S$ has norm one.

Let $E$ be a set of vertices whose intersection with every segment is empty or a segment. The coordinate projection $P_E$ is contractive on both $J$ and $X=J^*$. Its range on $J$ is the completion of $c_{00}(E)$ under the segment norm restricted to $E$, and $$\|P_Ex\|=\|x|_{P_EJ}\| \qquad (x\in X).$$ In particular these assertions apply to an ancestral set, its complement, a difference of nested ancestral sets, a descendant subtree, and an antichain. On an antichain the coordinate norm on either space is exactly the usual $\ell_2$ norm.
Let $x\in S_N$, let $(z_j)$ be weakly null, and suppose $N(z_j)\ge t>0$ for every $j$. For every $0<\gamma<\overline\delta_N(t)$, all sufficiently large $j$ satisfy $$N(x+z_j)>1+\gamma.$$

Suppose an infinite-dimensional real Banach space $(Z,\|\cdot\|)$ contains, for every positive integer $k$, vectors $(u_s)_{s\in\mathbb N^{\le k}}$ such that $$0<m\le\|u_s\|\le M,
 \qquad \|u_{s^\frown j}-u_s\|\ge c>0,$$ where $m,M,c$ are independent of $k$, and for each nonterminal $s$ the sequence $(u_{s^\frown j}-u_s)_j$ is weakly null against the whole continuous dual of $Z$. If $0<a\le b<\infty$ and $a\|z\|\le N(z)\le b\|z\|$, then $$\overline\delta_N\!\left(\frac{ac}{bM}\right)=0.$$ In particular the same conclusion holds at $ac/(2bM)$, and $Z$ admits no equivalent asymptotically uniformly convex norm.

If the finite component heights $h_i$ in Proposition 12 are unbounded, then every equivalent norm $N$ on $X_{\boldsymbol h}$ with $a\|x\|\le N(x)\le b\|x\|$ satisfies $$\overline\delta_N(a/b)=\overline\delta_N(a/(2b))=0.$$

The unit root-path vectors in $B_\infty$ have unit child increments which are weakly null among the children of each fixed vertex. Every sequence of distinct coordinate vectors is in fact weakly null. If $a\|\cdot\|\le N\le b\|\cdot\|$, with $0<a\le b<\infty$, then the one-sided asymptotic modulus of $N$ vanishes at $a/(2b)$ and at $a/b$. In particular, $B_\infty$ has no equivalent AUC norm. The same obstruction holds for the finite-height forest, using trees of arbitrarily large finite height.

In $B_\infty$, the root paths $h_v=d_{[o,v]}$ and the coordinates $e_v^*$ have norm one, and the children $(e_{v^\frown j}^*)_j$ of each fixed vertex are weakly null. If $a\|z\|\le N(z)\le b\|z\|$, with $0<a\le b<\infty$, then $\overline\delta_N(a/(2b))=0$.*

*More precisely, put $t_0=a/(2b)$, with $d,\varepsilon>0$ below. Each of the following assumptions would permit a finite-codimensional subspace and a child whose approximation error and growth factor satisfy the corresponding row: $$\begin{array}{c|c|c}
 \text{assumed positive lower bound}&
 \text{error less than}&\text{growth factor}\\\hline
 0<d<\overline\delta_N(t_0)&\min(a/2,ad/2)&1+d/2\rule{0pt}{13pt}\\
 2\varepsilon<\overline\delta_N(t_0)&
       \min(a/2,a\varepsilon/2)&1+\varepsilon/2\\
 d=\overline\delta_N(t_0)>0&\min(a/2,ad/4)&1+d/4
\end{array}$$ Here the error is $N(e_v^*-f)$ for the chosen child and its approximant $f$ in the finite-codimensional subspace. Growth is measured relative to the $N$-norm of the parent root-path vector.
For the infinite-height coordinate predual $B_\infty$ and the finite-height forest space $X$, $$\widehat\delta_Z(t)\ge\sqrt{1+t^2/12}-1\qquad(t>0).$$

If $x=P_Hx$ and $y=Q_Hy$, then $$\label{dir:primal:add:optimized}
 \max_{\pm}\|x\pm y\|\ge\sqrt{\|x\|^2+\|y\|^2/12}.$$ If $0<\sigma\le1$ and $w,Z_1,Z_2,\ldots\in X$ satisfy $\|w\pm Z_j\|\le1$ and $\|Z_j-Z_l\|\ge2\sigma$ for $j\ne l$, then $\|w\|\le1-\sigma^2/24$.

Suppose $x=P_Hx$, $\|x\|=1$, $y\in\ker P_H$, and $v=Q_Hv$, $\rho(v)\le1$, and $y(v)>\|y\|/2$. For every $s>0$, each of the following constructions produces an exterior test $w$ with $$|y(w)|>\|y\|/8,\qquad \rho(w)\le1,
 \qquad \rho(f+sw)^2\le1+3s^2,$$ where $f=P_Hf$ norms $x$ and the inward signs are chosen with full cone budgets $q_g$.*

1.  *Take the positive and negative cumulative parts globally, choose one by its total pairing, then retain one of the two groups of cones having the same prescribed inward sign.*

2.  *Form all four combinations of a cumulative positive/negative part and a prescribed inward-sign group, and select one by its pairing.*

3.  *Choose a cumulative part separately in each cone, orient it inward, then retain the cones on which the resulting pairings have one common sign.

For each $D\ge1$, there exists $c_D>0$ such that, if $x,z_i\in X$, $1\le\|x\|\le D$, $\|z_i\|\le2D$, and $\|z_i-z_j\|\ge1$ for distinct indices in an infinite sequence, then some $i$ satisfies $\max_{\pm}\|x\pm z_i\|>\|x\|+c_D$.

For a finite ancestral $H$, $x=P_Hx$, and arbitrary $y\in X$ with $\|x\pm y\|\le R$, one has $$\label{eq:atomic-tail}
 \|Q_Hy\|\le(\sqrt2+\sqrt6)\sqrt{R(R-\|x\|)}.$$
For the specified dual norm on $X$, $$\overline\theta_X(t)\ge\frac{\sqrt{1+t^2/4}-1}{2}\qquad(t>0).$$

The coordinate identity satisfies $a(x)=q(x)=\|x\|$ on $c_{00}(\mathcal F)$ and extends to surjective linear isometries $$X_a=X_q=X=J^*.$$ The finite unit balls and completed atomic ball are therefore exactly those of Lemma 7 and Corollary 8.
Let $(r_j)$ be a finite or countable family of incomparable vertices, and put $U_j=\{v:r_j\preceq v\}$. For $x\in X_a$ supported in $\bigcup_jU_j$, $$a(x)^2=\sum_j a(P_{U_j}x)^2.$$

Two represented atoms $A,B$, tested against the same $p$, satisfy $$\label{stab:coef:head-conflict-eq}
 2\sum_{g:s_g(A)s_g(B)<0}|s_g(A)s_g(B)|\le D(A)+D(B).$$ There are two direct proofs: one discards a suffix of the longer head, and the other splits the longer segment into two pieces.

Let $A$ have a finite law of represented atoms and suppose $\mathbb E L(A)\le k$, where $k\ge0$. Write $$\beta=\|\mathbb E c(A)\|_2,\qquad
 M_c=(\mathbb E|c_g(A)|)_g,\qquad
 M_s=(\mathbb E|s_g(A)|)_g.$$ Then $$\begin{aligned}
 \|\mathbb E s(A)\|_2&\le\beta+\sqrt{2k},
       \label{stab:coef:mean-head}\\
 \|M_s\|_2^2&\le(\beta+\sqrt{2k})^2+4k,
       \label{stab:coef:absolute-head}\\
 \|M_c\|_2&\le\sqrt{(\beta+\sqrt{2k})^2+4k}+\sqrt{2k},
       \label{stab:coef:via-head}\\
 \|M_c\|_2^2&\le\beta^2+4k+4\sqrt{2k}.
       \label{stab:coef:via-products}
\end{aligned}$$ The last inequality is obtained directly from the original products, whereas the preceding one first controls the signs of the head sums.

Let $G$ be a finite antichain and, for each $g\in G$, let $$f_g=\sum_j a_{g,j}d_{[g,w_{g,j}]},\qquad M_g=\sum_j|a_{g,j}|,$$ where every sum is finite. Then $$\label{stab:sign:absolute-masses} \left\|\sum_g f_g\right\|\le\|(M_g)_g\|_2.$$ If the nonzero coefficients have one common sign for each fixed $g$, then $$\label{stab:sign:rooted-equality} \left\|\sum_g f_g\right\| =\left(\sum_g|f_g(e_g)|^2\right)^{1/2}.$$ Consequently, adding another rooted mixture with the same sign at each $g$ cannot decrease the norm.* *In particular, for a finite law of represented atoms, put $M_c=(\mathbb E|c_g(A)|)_g$. For any real random variable $\theta$ with $|\theta|\le1$, $$\label{stab:coef:tail-assembly-eq} \|\mathbb E(\theta C(A))\|\le\|M_c\|_2.$$ If the law is an equal mixture of two laws with expectations $\mathbb E_+,\mathbb E_-$, then $$\label{stab:coef:conditional-assembly} \|\mathbb E_\pm C(A)\| \le\|(\mathbb E_\pm|c_g(A)|)_g\|_2\le2\|M_c\|_2.$$ The same estimates pass to norm limits of finite rooted mixtures when their absolute-mass vectors converge in $\ell_2$. In particular, countably many roots are permitted when their masses are square summable and the series at each root is absolutely summable.
For either coordinate model, $$\widehat\delta_Z(t)\ge t^2/1024\qquad(0<t<1).$$ For every $t>0$ and every $0<e<1/4$ with $25\sqrt e<t$, one also has $\widehat\delta_Z(t)\ge e/2$.

For every $t>0$, put $$\label{molw:rho}
 \omega(t)=\frac{\sqrt{1+4(t/C)^2}-1}{2},\qquad C=\sqrt2+\sqrt6.$$ Then the averaged asymptotic modulus of $B_\infty$ satisfies $\widehat\delta_{B_\infty}(t)\ge\omega(t)/2>0$. The bound holds when the cofinite infimum allows every perturbation direction of norm at least one.

In the forest space $X=J^*$, let $H$ be finite and ancestral, $x=P_Hx$, $y=Q_Hy$, and $x\pm y\in B_X$. Put $d=1-\|x\|$. For every $\varepsilon>0$, the finite atomic approximation argument gives $$\label{mol:closed-hull-error}
 \|y\|\le e_\varepsilon+
 \sqrt{e_\varepsilon^2+4(d+\varepsilon)},\qquad
 e_\varepsilon=\varepsilon+\sqrt{2(d+\varepsilon)}.$$ Consequently $\|y\|\le(\sqrt2+\sqrt6)\sqrt d$.

Let $H$ be finite and ancestral, $x=P_Hx$, $P_Hz=0$, and $\|x\pm z\|\le1$. Put $d=1-\|x\|\in[0,1]$ and $$\omega_{\mathrm{coef}}(d)=2\bigl(\sqrt{2d}+\sqrt{6d+4\sqrt{2d}}\bigr) \qquad(d\ge0).$$ The original coefficients give both $$\begin{aligned} \|z\|&\le(\sqrt{12}+2\sqrt2)\sqrt d, \label{stab:coef:square-root}\\ \|z\|&\le\omega_{\mathrm{coef}}(d). \label{stab:coef:fourth-root} \end{aligned}$$ More generally, if $0\le d_0<1$ and $\|x\|\ge1-d_0$, the right side of [stab:coef:fourth-root] may be replaced by $\omega_{\mathrm{coef}}(d_0)$.

In the forest space $X$, suppose $H$ is finite and ancestor-closed, $x=P_Hx$, $y=Q_Hy$, and $\|x+y\|,\|x-y\|\le1$. Then $$\|y\|\le g(1-\|x\|),\qquad
 g(s)=\sqrt{2s}+\sqrt{6s+4\sqrt{2s}}\quad(s\ge0).$$

If $x=P_Hx$ has norm one, $P_Hy=0$, and $\|x\pm y\|\le R$ for $R\ge1$, then $$\label{stab:coef:unit-head-lens-eq}
 \|y\|\le(\sqrt{12}+2\sqrt2)\sqrt{R(R-1)}.$$

Let $H$ be finite and ancestral, $x=P_Hx$ have norm one, and $P_Hy=0$. For $d>0$, the assumptions $\|x\pm y\|\le1+d$ imply $$\label{stab:coef:approximate-tail-eq}
 \|y\|\le(1+d)(7\sqrt2+4)\sqrt d.$$ In particular, $\|y\|\le32\sqrt d$ when $0<d\le1$.

For $0<\delta<1$ and every unit $x\in X$, one can choose a finite ancestor-closed $H$ such that $\|x\pm y\|\le1+\delta$ implies $$\|Qy\|\le\eta(\delta):=(1+\delta)
 \left\{2\sqrt{(2\delta+\sqrt{6\delta})^2
                    +4(3\delta+\sqrt{6\delta})}
             +2\sqrt{6\delta}+\delta\right\}.$$ In particular $\eta(\delta)\to0$ as $\delta\downarrow0$.

For $0<t<1$, each of the following conclusions holds.*

1.  *If $e>0$ satisfies $$(\sqrt{12}+2\sqrt2)\sqrt{(1+e)e}<t/2,$$ then $\widehat\delta_Z(t)\ge e/4$.*

2.  *If $0<c<1$, $R=1+4c$, and $R\omega_{\mathrm{coef}}(5c/R)<t$, then $\widehat\delta_Z(t)\ge c$.*

3.  *If $d>0$, $3d<1$, and $(1+2d)\omega_{\mathrm{coef}}(3d)<t$, then $\widehat\delta_Z(t)\ge d/2$.*

4.  *The completed atomic-ball route gives $\widehat\delta_Z(t)\ge t^2/16384$.

Fix a primal unit vector $z$ supported on $H$, and a finite probability distribution of represented atoms $A_\omega=\sum_Ic_{\omega I}\mathbf1_I$, with probabilities $p_\omega$. Write $$b_{\omega I}=z(I),\qquad
 L_\omega=1-\sum_Ib_{\omega I}^2,\qquad
 B_\omega=\sum_Ib_{\omega I}Q\mathbf1_I.$$ At each gate let $P_g$ and $M_g$ be the positive and absolute negative coefficient masses in $\mathbb E B$. Then $$\label{molb:eq:matching-capacity}
 \sum_g\min(P_g,M_g)^2\le\mathbb E L.$$

Let $X=J^*$ be the finite-height forest space defined by [eq:segment-norm], with the atomic and polar norm identifications of Proposition 31. For a finite ancestor-closed set $A\subset\mathcal F$, let $P_A$ be coordinate restriction on $X$ and let $Q_A=I-P_A$. If $$P_Ax=x,\qquad Q_Ay=y,\qquad \|x+y\|,\|x-y\|\le1,$$ then, with $d=1-\|x\|$, $$\label{molx:minimum-conclusion} \|y\|\le(\sqrt6+2\sqrt2)\sqrt d\le6\sqrt d.$$

Let $A$ be a nonempty finite ancestral set and let $x,y\in B_\infty$ with $x=P_Ax$ and $P_Ay=0$. For every $\varepsilon\ge0$, $$\max\{\|x+y\|,\|x-y\|\}\le1,
 \qquad \|x\|\ge1-\varepsilon
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \|y\|\le (\sqrt2+\sqrt{10})\sqrt\varepsilon.$$
Let $b_L=\sqrt{L^2-1}+2\sqrt{(1-L^{-2})/2}$ for $L>1$. If $0<t<1$ and $L$ is chosen so that $3b_L<t$, then $$\widehat\delta_Z(t)\ge (L-1)/8>0.$$

In the forest space $X$, let $h=P_Hh$, $P_Hu=0$, and $h+u,h-u\in B_X$. Then $$\label{stab:sign:forest-parent-bound}
 \|u\|\le3(\sqrt2+2)\sqrt{1-\|h\|}.$$

Let $x=P_Hx$, $\|x\|=1$, and $y\in\ker P_H$. Put $C_{\mathrm{ex}}=2+3\sqrt2$. For every $\delta>0$, with $\eta=\delta/(1+\delta)$, $$\label{stab:sign:exit-lens-bound}
